title: Telling the request what changed
question: How much cheaper is a slider release's request to the evaluation worker on hazelgrove/hazel#2635 after two commits that keep the request's projection of the statics and let the per-item statics say which keys changed, and can the change be carried to #2469, dev and #2597?
runtime: node, on a laptop, with Hazel's test build (dune's dev profile); one probe (PortData) built into the test suite of all four builds
runs: each build run twice, interleaved. Each series analyses a program cold, then edits one integer literal five or six times as the editor edits a model, every id kept. Edit 1 of each series is the first after a cold start (the engine warming up): it is left out of the medians and kept in the tables.

measures.statics: ms: the statics after the edit
measures.projection: ms: building the request's projection of the statics
measures.request: ms: the request in all (projection + hashing + encoding)
measures.new nodes: count: objects of the new projection that are not objects of the last one
measures.nodes copied: count: arrays an encoding output holds that are not references
measures.rebuild, walk, as built: ms, test programs: rebuilding the projection, walking the two statics maps, and the change as built

times: performance.now() around each part; medians over edits 2 on

raw_files.data/data013.tsv: the probe's rows, tab-separated, no header. First the run's tag (<build>-<run>), then either: DATA branch program where pos items edit statics rebuild walk keyed new_nodes (the test programs), or SLIDER branch slide slider pos items edit statics proj hash enc new_prog new_info (the Livelit Playground slides). Times in ms.
raw_files.data/enc013.tsv: the encoding, split: ENC branch slide slider pos items edit t_program t_info copies_program copies_info (ms, then counts of arrays copied)
